decisions.reason: Liquid-path cleanability is independently addressed by the cleaning and trapped-liquid clauses in message 176; broadening electrical isolation does not further change its state.
The bowl-removal Requirement already has a same-message scope update from the independent sanitation clause; the electrical-isolation change adds no bowl-removal behavior.
The existing requirement to prevent liquid leaking into the base remains valid unchanged; the source decision broadens electrical isolation without changing the plumbing seal requirement.
Food-contact materials are independently specified in message 176 and already have a matching Event; electrical isolation does not alter the approved materials or coverage.
The whisk-removal Requirement already reflects the independent sanitation and food-service scope from message 176; liquid-electrical isolation does not change its removal behavior.
The source decision does not specifically change spout removability, and the reference to other removable components does not necessarily identify the spout.
Maintenance access is independently reaffirmed by message 176 and already has a matching Event; the electrical-isolation modification requires no additional maintenance-access change.
Separating liquids from electrical components does not change the controlled-pour, anti-drip, texture-preservation, or dispensing-path requirements.
Documentation retention and contents are independently introduced in message 176; the electrical-isolation decision does not alter that deliverable.
The source decision imposes physical liquid-electrical separation but does not change the solenoid actuation mechanism or button-control behavior.
Liquid isolation does not change the required electrical load headroom, simultaneous loads, or cooling capacity.
The source decision does not change the required wiring-plan detail level; the separate request to retain a wiring layout belongs to the maintenance-documentation Requirement.
